case_title: SANTOSH S/O SHANKAR PAWAR v. STATE OF MAHARASHTRA
aggravating_circumstances: Bride burning, absence of provocation, act of pouring kerosene and setting fire
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 IPC, sentenced to life imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000/-
neutral_facts: The accused, a daily wages worker, married a woman shortly before the incident. The couple resided in a rented house due to poverty. On the day of the incident, the accused questioned the victim about her return time, suspecting her fidelity. The accused assaulted her with fists and kicks, then poured kerosene over her and set her on fire. The victim suffered severe burns and later succumbed to her injuries. The victim's dying declaration, along with the testimony of her family members and neighbors, established the accused's actions. A post-mortem report confirmed the cause of death as shock and septicaemia from the burns. The accused attempted to extinguish the fire by pouring water on the victim, but this act was not considered a mitigating factor as it was seen as an attempt to conceal his guilt.
